verdict.rationale: Plaid Link is documented as Plaid's own client-side drop-in component that users interact with to link their bank accounts, so developers don't build institution UI themselves. The Link flow can also be customized from the Dashboard. The pack does not document the server-side session creation step or the token returned to the app after a successful link, so the end-to-end flow is only partly evidenced. Missing for 10: documentation of server-side session/link-token creation, documentation of the token returned and exchanged after Link completes in production, independent hands-on corroboration of the full flow.

support.subject: As a developer, I can let a user connect their bank with a drop-in hosted flow — create a session server-side, open the widget, and get back a token for the connected account — without building institution UI myself

citations.quote: Plaid Link is the client-side component that your users will interact with in order to link their accounts to Plaid and allow you to access their accounts via the Plaid API.
You can customize parts of Link's flow straight from the Dashboard.
This endpoint allows you to generate a public_token for an arbitrary institution ID, initial products, and test credentials.
